Text 1
Some parents worry that playing video games harms children's ability to pay attention.

Text 2
In a study of 2,000 children, those who played puzzle-based video games for an hour a day performed as well on attention tests as children who did not play, and slightly better on tests of spatial reasoning.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the parents' concern in Text 1?
choices: By noting that one study found no harm to attention from playing puzzle-based games
By agreeing that children should not play any video games at all during the school week
By arguing that video games improve children's attention more than any other activity does
By recommending that parents limit their children to fewer than thirty minutes of games a day
steps: Text 2: puzzle-game players did as well on attention tests (and better on spatial reasoning).
So Text 2 would point to evidence that attention wasn't harmed, at least for puzzle games.
Text 2 doesn't call for a ban, doesn't claim games beat every activity, and makes no time recommendation.
key: Base the response only on what Text 2's evidence shows.
